2607.27167.title: SpecFirst: Behavioral Specification Elicitation as a First-Class Step in Agent-Based Program Synthesis from Scratch
2607.27167.paper_summary: LLM-based agents excel at software engineering tasks where an existing codebase provides context, but constructing a program from scratch remains fundamentally harder. Recent benchmarks such as ProgramBench quantify this gap: given only natural-language documentation and an execute-only binary as a behavioral oracle, even frontier models solve fewer than 1% of instances. Existing frameworks conflate documentation reading, behavioral exploration, and code synthesis into a single pass, causing agents to probe insufficiently, lose behavioral intent as context drifts, and propagate early misinterpretations into the final implementation. Inspired by classical requirements engineering, we argue that behavioral specification elicitation should be a first-class phase that precedes implementation. We present SpecFirst, a two-stage framework that forces the specification elicitation before code synthesis. A dedicated spec agent first probes the binary and combines observations with documentation into a structured specification. Next, a code synthesis agent then uses this specification to drive implementation. This decomposition resolves documentation ambiguities before coding begins and provides a stable behavioral reference throughout synthesis. We evaluate SpecFirst on all 200 ProgramBench instances across four models spanning two families and an order of magnitude of capability. SpecFirst consistently outperforms the single-loop baseline, improving test pass rates by 6.9%-21.3% and binary exploration coverage by 9.4%-18.5%, all statistically significant. Behavioral analysis on code synthesis further shows that a prior specification enables earlier and more sustained code construction. Our results demonstrate that an explicit requirements-engineering phase is an effective paradigm for from-scratch program construction.
2607.27167.paper_summary_zh: LLM 基礎的代理在已有代碼庫提供上下文的軟體工程任務中表現優異，但從頭構建程式仍然根本上更難。最近的基準測試，例如 ProgramBench，量化了這一差距：僅根據自然語言文檔和作為行為神諭的執行專用二進位檔，即使是前沿模型也只能解決不到 1% 的實例。現有框架將文檔閱讀、行為探索和代碼合成混為一談，導致代理探查不足，隨著上下文漂移而失去行為意圖，並將早期的誤解傳播到最終實現中。受到傳統需求工程的啟發，我們主張行為規範引導應該是實現之前的一個重要階段。我們提出了 SpecFirst，一個兩階段的框架，強制在代碼合成之前進行規範引導。專門的規範代理首先探查二進位檔，並將觀察結果與文檔結合成結構化的規範。接著，代碼合成代理使用這一規範來驅動實現。這一分解在編碼開始之前解決了文檔的模糊性，並在整個合成過程中提供了穩定的行為參考。我們在跨越兩個家族和一個數量級能力的四個模型上對所有 200 個 ProgramBench 實例評估了 SpecFirst。SpecFirst 始終優於單循環基準，提高了測試通過率 6.9%-21.3% 和二進位探索覆蓋率 9.4%-18.5%，且均具有統計顯著性。對代碼合成的行為分析進一步顯示，先前的規範使得更早且更持續的代碼構建成為可能。我們的結果表明，明確的需求工程階段是從頭構建程式的有效範式。
